case: Rayphand v. Sablan / Torres v. Sablan
result: Affirmed, 8–1; direct appellate jurisdiction sustained unanimously.
reconciled_start: ## Rayphand v. Sablan / Torres v. Sablan — December 13, 1999
reconciled_end: ## Steamfitters Local Union No. 420 Welfare Fund v. Philip Morris, Inc. — January 10, 2000
form: One signed plenary opinion on direct appeal, with severable jurisdiction and merits portions. The Court resolves the actual Covenant allocation through a confined territorial accommodation, not a summary denial of review. The eight-Associate merits opinion and Stone's distinct equality ground require a separate dissent. Form and R1–R3 precede assignment.
assignment_basis: Stone supports jurisdiction but dissents from the merits affirmance. Stevens is the senior participating Associate in the eight-Justice merits coalition and assigns the lead opinion. Section 8's mandatory Chief balance pool does not bind this Associate assignment; the actual authored lead nevertheless counts.
compatibility: All eight Associates join the confined accommodation and affirmance; all nine support the direct-appeal jurisdiction ground. Stone joins jurisdiction only and dissents from the merits and remedy, seeking reversal and a locally designed constitutional remedy with transition. No six- or five-Justice equality coalition survives final reconciliation. No historical undisclosed ballot or rationale is imported. The supplied exact Covenant provisions clarify the statutory interaction without changing Stone's stated constitutional objection to federal approval of the inequality.
kernel: One direct appeal, not two proceedings. The October 18, November 15 and December 13 calendar markers are authorized scheduling premises. Adopt the minimum routine premise of full merits briefing at the November 15 submission; do not represent an unverified oral argument. The source-supported three-judge District Court denied requested injunctive relief on the merits after hearing. Title 48 makes the relevant Title 28 provisions applicable; §1253 review and §2284 panel requirements are adjudicated expressly. The source's December filing corroborates preexisting May/July procedural events, not its own filing before December 13. The Covenant requires equal municipal representation in one chamber; the CNMI Constitution, rather than the Covenant itself, supplies three senators for each of three districts. Effective earlier Records are Flippo, Lesage, Fiore and Drye. Their search, admissions, certification and tax-lien holdings change no Covenant, jurisdiction or territorial-equality premise. Paul and United Reporting have no effective event or authorship count; their unresolved matters supply no authority here.
stone: The approved October 31, 2026 position reaches this designated direct appeal, supports the personal equal-voting-weight claim and requires reversal of the permanent extreme inequality in a general legislature. Stone joins the jurisdiction ground but cannot join the territorial accommodation. His dissent preserves constitutional territorial equality without equating territories and States in every respect. He would allow political branches to choose a lawful design, followed by a remedial court's transition/election determination; he dictates no seat total, voids no past enactments and invalidates no unrelated Covenant provision. No fallback supplies a merits position.
continuity: The challenged equal-island Senate allocation remains effective under the confined constitutional accommodation. Judicial review remains available; §902 is not an exclusive remedy. Stone's published dissent preserves the noncontrolling proposition that the general legislature's extreme vote inequality cannot be justified by the founding bargain and that locally selected reform with lawful transition is required. No new map, election or invalidation of prior legislation follows.
sources: The clean Rayphand validation and copied official Covenant/Title 48 provisions govern. The complete lower opinion and official jurisdictional recitations support the panel, noticed/heard injunction request, merits denial and direct-appeal timing; the unrecovered convening order and full panel roster are not invented. The reported census populations—38,932 for Saipan/northern islands, 2,118 for Tinian/Aguigan, and 2,295 for Rota—are judicial recitations, not independent census work or voter-registration counts. The final reconciliation identifies its qualitative corrections and preserves the distinction between a later unexplained historical institutional result and individual votes.

blocks.Event: Rayphand v. Sablan / Torres v. Sablan, No. 99-475. Merits decision, December 13, 1999. Submitted on full merits briefing November 15, 1999. On direct appeal from the three-judge District Court for the Northern Mariana Islands. The two caption forms identify one appeal. The question is whether the federally approved Covenant may preserve equal island representation in the Commonwealth's general legislative Senate despite the substantial population disparities.
blocks.Participation: Chief Justice Stone-Zsela and Justices Stevens, O'Connor, Scalia, Kennedy, Souter, Thomas, Ginsburg, and Breyer participate.
blocks.Public Action: The Court exercises direct appellate jurisdiction and affirms the judgment rejecting the challenge to the equal-island Senate allocation.
blocks.Judgment & Remedy: Affirmed, 8–1. Supporting: Stevens, O'Connor, Scalia, Kennedy, Souter, Thomas, Ginsburg, and Breyer. Opposing: Stone-Zsela, who would reverse the challenged inequality and remand for a constitutional remedy. All nine sustain direct appellate jurisdiction. The denial of the requested injunction remains in place. No new district map, seat count, special election, ouster of incumbents or invalidation of past legislation is ordered.

blocks.Holdings:
**I. The direct appeal is within the Court's jurisdiction.** The heard denial of injunctive relief by the required three-judge court in this Commonwealth legislative-apportionment action is reviewable under 28 U.S.C. §1253. Covenant §902's intergovernmental consultation procedure does not displace these residents' judicial remedy for asserted personal vote dilution.

**Authority:** The jurisdiction portion of {AUTHOR}'s opinion has all nine Justices' direct support.

**Controlling explanation:** Sections 1821(c) and 1824 of Title 48 apply the relevant federal judicial provisions to the Commonwealth; Calero-Toledo supports treating an autonomous territorial commonwealth's government as a State for the relevant three-judge-court function. Section 2284 applies to this general legislative-apportionment challenge, and the actual panel, hearing and merits denial satisfy the direct-review route. The two Saipan residents allege diminished weight of their own votes. Section 902 establishes political consultation, while §202 expressly preserves judicial consistency review. Neither a new certiorari grant nor an exclusive political-remedy rule is needed.

**II. The particular federal territorial settlement may preserve one equal-island chamber.** The constitutional requirements for this unincorporated territory permit Congress's express accommodation of equal municipal representation in one chamber alongside a population-based other chamber. This specific protected territorial arrangement does not violate equal protection merely because it would fail the population rule governing both chambers of an ordinary State legislature.

**Authority:** The merits portion of {AUTHOR}'s opinion is joined by all seven other Associates. Stone-Zsela dissents from this rule and its application.

**Controlling explanation:** The Court recognizes the severe voting disparity and the Senate's general legislative power. Reynolds and Board of Estimate explain why those facts would defeat ordinary state or local geographical representation, but they did not adjudicate this distinct federal territorial settlement. The territorial constitutional framework, reflected in Verdugo-Urquidez, requires attention to the particular institutional relationship while retaining constitutional protection for residents. Covenant §203(c) expressly requires equal municipal representation. Section 501(a) makes Fourteenth Amendment §1 applicable as if the Commonwealth were a State, to the extent it does not apply of its own force; §501(b) preserves the validity of, and Congress's power to consent to, §203. The statutory terms defeat simple transplantation through §501(a), although Congress's constitutional power still requires independent decision. Here the expressly protected allocation, local self-government and population-based other chamber support the confined accommodation. Section 105 gives mutual consent legal significance but does not by itself let a bargain waive individual rights. Neither the national Senate analogy nor proof that another map is technically possible decides the constitutional question.

**Limits:** The Court holds neither that equal protection is inapplicable in territories nor that every territorial departure survives. An ordinary State or municipality cannot invoke this founding arrangement as permission for the same inequality. No universal historical-bargain exception, numerical deviation threshold, wholesale endorsement of every territorial precedent, or finding that union would otherwise have been impossible is adopted.
blocks.Precedent Treatment: Calero-Toledo v. Pearson Yacht Leasing Co. is applied by analogy to the autonomous commonwealth and three-judge review channel. Reynolds v. Sims and Board of Estimate v. Morris retain their state/local population-equality force and are distinguished by the particular territorial settlement; they are not overruled. United States v. Verdugo-Urquidez supplies the context-sensitive territorial framework, not a prior holding about this Senate. El Vocero confirms that territory is not an automatic exemption from an applicable constitutional guarantee. Shaw and the Miller group preserve actual unequal-participation claims but do not decide this territorial merits issue. The lower-court Atalig and Wabol analyses are considered within their respective settings, not elevated into prior Supreme Court holdings on this legislature.
blocks.Law After Decision: The Commonwealth's equal municipal representation in one Senate chamber remains constitutional within the specific federally approved arrangement. The population-based other chamber and protected territorial structure are material to that result. The ordinary state/local population rule and judicial review of territorial constitutional claims remain in force.
blocks.Separate Writings: Chief Justice Stone-Zsela dissents from the merits and remedy while joining jurisdiction. He would apply the individual protection against severely unequal voting weight to this general territorial legislature. Reynolds supplies the distinction between geographical representation and individual political equality; Board of Estimate directs attention to the body's actual governmental powers. Smaller-island protection is substantial, but federal approval and an earlier generation's bargain do not by themselves justify permanently unequal individual votes. The national Senate rests on the Constitution's own allocation, unlike this congressional settlement. Flores de Otero confirms a constitutional foundation for territorial equality, though every territorial setting need not follow identical rules. Stone-Zsela would reverse only the challenged inequality and permit the political branches to choose a lawful design, with the remedial court addressing transition and election timing without indefinitely preserving the violation. He would not dictate a seat total, invalidate unrelated Covenant terms or void past enactments. His proposed remedy would not invalidate autonomous local island institutions.
blocks.Procedure After Action: The District Court's merits judgment and denial of the requested apportionment relief stand. The challenged allocation remains in effect; no special remedial proceeding or election is directed.
blocks.Source Notes: The judgment below is 95 F. Supp. 2d 1133. The Covenant and the Commonwealth Constitution supply distinct allocation provisions. The reported census figures establish population disparity, not an exact voter-registration ratio. Review proceeds on the stated full-briefing submission schedule. The official jurisdictional recitations support the prior panel and appeal events without supplying a full panel roster or the original convening order.
